Completed: solution.py (self-contained, numpy-only, deterministic — re-run verified byte-identical) executed once and produced all 18 required artifacts under ./results/.

DIAGNOSIS (results/diagnosis/)
- picard_data.csv: header singular_value,fourier_coeff,picard_ratio + 222 rows.
- diagnosis_report.md with structured fields: noise_estimate: 0.0293, effective_rank: 23, dpc_judgment: does_not_hold.
- Key findings: K 222×222, ||K||2=1.0, ||K||F=1.943; singular values decay geometrically (s_i/s_{i+1}=1.166 constant, s_19=0.054, s_29=0.0116, cond≈5.7e14); energy 99.79% in top 20; Picard ratios plateau O(1) to i≈30 then explode (max ~800) → DPC does not hold; roughness fit Var(yhat_i)=τ²s_i²+σ² gives τ=1.214 (x is rough, ||x||~18). Noise σ̂=0.0293 (half-normal tail estimate; chi-square 159.7/162 consistent; Ljung-Box Q=0.0008; flat block variances) → WHITE, so Tikhonov applied to raw y, no whitening. effective_rank=23 = #{s_i ≥ σ̂} (alternatives: 99%-energy 15, entropy 8.9).

SOLUTIONS (all parameters data-only)
- method_a = tikhonov: α* = 0.01217 by exact LOO-CV (interior min, flat valley 0.003–0.03); cross-checks: L-curve knee α=0.0172, Wiener scale σ̂/τ=0.0241 (agree within factor ~2). ||x||=6.93, ||y−Kx||=0.400, effective dim 25.9. lcurve_data.csv: 200-row alpha sweep (alpha,residual_norm,solution_norm). Note: GCV is unusable for Tikhonov here (collapses to α→∞, prefers x=0 — documented).
- method_b = tsvd: r* = 26 by GCV; cross-checks: exact LOO-CV r=28, L-curve knee r=30 (all within 4). ||x||=6.80, ||r||=0.405.
- method_c = cgls: m* = 9 by L-curve knee restricted to the pre-noise-amplification region (||x_m|| ≤ √n·τ ≈ 18); cross-check: noise-floor stopping m=6 (agree within 3). ||x||=3.51, ||r||=0.443, effective dim 3.7. CGLS LOO-CV diverges (leverages→1) and CGLS GCV is degenerate (min at m=1) — documented.
- method_a/b/c directories verified byte-identical to tikhonov/tsvd/cgls.

COMPARISON (results/comparison/)
- comparison_report.md: per-method residual norm, solution norm, effective dimension, parameter sensitivity (Tikhonov α×2/÷2 → 39%/69%; TSVS r±2/±5 → 49–76%; CGLS m±5 → 52–85%), criterion agreement, and justification.
- Recommended: Tikhonov α=0.01217 (written to recommended_solution.csv, one column, no header). Justification: (1) parameter from exact LOO-CV with stable interior minimum; (2) soft filter matches the theoretical Wiener/MMSE form for a rough x, α* within factor ~2 of the data-estimated optimum σ̂/τ=0.024; (3) TSVS r=26 independently confirms the same effective dimension; (4) CGLS early stopping least trustworthy (Krylov-governed trajectory, degenerate CV criteria, strongest regularization).

EVIDENCE OF EXECUTION: solution.py ran (exit 0); console summary: sigma_hat=0.0293, effective_rank=23, dpc=does_not_hold, Tikhonov α*=0.01217 (||x||=6.932, ||r||=0.3998), TSVS r*=26 (||x||=6.798, ||r||=0.4053), CGLS m*=9 (||x||=3.509, ||r||=0.4433). All 18 files present, nonempty, format-checked (222-row single-column x files, single-number reg_param files, 3-column picard CSV with header, 200-row lcurve CSV, structured fields on own lines in diagnosis report). Second run reproduced byte-identical outputs.

LIMITATIONS: x is rough (τ≈1.2), so all regularized solutions are strong underestimates of the true ||x||≈18 — modes beyond i≈25 are unrecoverable; Tikhonov sensitivity to α/2 is 69% (soft filter at the information limit); CGLS m-selection relies on heuristics (L-curve knee + noise floor) because its CV criteria are degenerate; the whitening decision rests on the whiteness tests (Ljung-Box, block variances), which passed but have finite-sample uncertainty.
